summary: Workers and lifts are technically rendered, but the operator perceives them as invisible because (a) selectedFloor is never initialized from the URL, so the floor inspector stays in its 'Click a floor' placeholder even when ?floor=42 is in the URL; (b) the lift shafts are drawn at 0.36 opacity blue lines on a dark gradient background and the 9 capsules carry generic initials with no lift identity or status; (c) Floor 42 (and trading floors 41/43) have no entries in qsb_worker_room_assignments because the V1 generator only emitted rooms for admin floors 30/36/38/44/45/47/49/52; (d) tower-zoomed view does not paint per-floor density badges, so the 1191 canonical workers reduce to invisible totals; (e) the dashboard sidebar 'Workers' panel reads /api/unified.workers which only contains 64 legacy sandbox seeds, producing the misleading '64 visible' line.

questions.why_1191_workers_counted_but_not_visible: The exterior renderer shows aggregate counts only. There is no per-floor density badge on the SVG floor slabs that summarizes workers-per-floor. Individual labels are deliberately suppressed at the zoomed-out level to avoid 1191 unreadable labels.
questions.why_only_64_visible: 64 is the length of the /api/unified.workers list, which contains the legacy sandbox seeds (market_scout, oanda_executor, etc.). The 'Workers' right-rail panel reads /api/unified and prints len(workers). It is not a render cap — it is the cardinality of a legacy registry.
questions.visible_worker_budget: qsb_worker_visible_scene_state.json sets interior_workers_per_floor_when_selected=8 and exterior_per_floor_badges_count=80 (5 classes * 16 sample floors). There is no hardcoded 64 cap anywhere in the renderer.
questions.is_64_a_cap: No. 64 is the cardinality of /api/unified.workers (legacy seed list).
questions.why_floor_42_interior_empty: Floor 42 has 2 canonical V1 workers but qsb_worker_room_assignments.by_floor_room contains entries only for floors 30/36/38/44/45/47/49/52. The Binance trading floor (42), OANDA (41), and Stocks (43) were never given room assignments.
questions.why_inspector_says_click_a_floor_when_ur: Neither cockpit.js nor qsb_3d_app.js parses URLSearchParams. window.QSB.selectedFloor is initialized to null and only set when a 'qsb:pick' event is dispatched (i.e. a click on an SVG floor slab). URL parameter ?floor=42 is ignored.
questions.why_9_lifts_not_visibly_rendered: qsb_tower_2d.js does draw 9 lift shafts (line 332 buildShafts) and 9 capsules (line 402 buildCapsules), but: stroke rgba(80,170,240,0.36) on dark navy background is near-invisible; capsule labels are 2-letter initials with no lift_id/status/current_floor; no per-lift indicator strip is drawn at the side of the tower; idle capsules sit parked without any IDLE label.
questions.which_function_renders_lifts: qsb_tower_2d.js :: buildShafts() + buildCapsules() inside the SVG renderer. Babylon scene also renders capsules in qsb_scene.js.
questions.which_function_renders_workers: qsb_tower_2d.js + qsb_rebuild_workers.js (in-slab grid dots for selected floor) + qsb_3d_workers.js (named rows in right-side interior panel).
questions.which_function_renders_selected_floor_in: qsb_3d_workers.js :: renderSelectedFloorInterior(floor, cache). This requires window.QSB.selectedFloor to be non-null. It is never set from URL.
questions.which_state_variable_is_failing: window.QSB.selectedFloor — never initialized from window.location.search, only set via click event.

current_render_inventory.lift_shaft_glow: rgba(110,210,255,0.22) width 5.0 — barely visible on dark background
current_render_inventory.lift_capsule_labels: 2-letter initials hardcoded ['MS','SW','RS','PS','KC','LC','OM','SI','CA'] — not bound to lifts.json registry
